items.summary: According to a Wall Street Journal report, Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners—including Dell and Super Micro—to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period while it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements. The move comes as Chinese companies have reportedly been accessing Nvidia chips remotely from data centers in these countries, a practice the U.S. Commerce Department closed earlier this month—described by the Journal as done grudgingly. The Institute for Progress estimates that remote data centers like these supply roughly 24% of China's AI computing power.
items.title: Nvidia Pauses Chip Shipments to Southeast Asia Over U.S. Export Concerns

items.summary: Leaders from the 21 euro-using European countries filled three top posts at the European Central Bank, which sets borrowing costs for the 359 million people in the eurozone. European Council President Antonio Costa announced on X that the body agreed to the appointments at a summit in Brussels. The central appointment is Adão de Cos, former head of the Spanish central bank and age 55, who served on the ECB rate-setting council from 2018 to 2024 through his role as Spain's central banker. His nomination still must pass review by the European Parliament and the ECB governing council, though those steps are described as formalities. Commerzbank analysts reviewed de Cos's speeches and concluded they suggest he is among the monetary policy doves—policymakers who lean toward lower rates to support growth—which positions him at a time when several European governments face heavy debt loads and rising borrowing costs.
items.title: Ex-Spain Central Bank Head Named Next ECB Chief

items.summary: Apple announced it will open its first store in Hyderabad, Telangana—"Apple Kukatpally," located at Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall—with the opening scheduled for December 10. This expansion brings Apple's total retail footprint in India to seven stores: Apple BKC and Apple Borivali in Mumbai; Apple Saket and Apple Noida in Delhi NCR; Apple Hebbal in Bengaluru; Apple Koregaon Park in Pune; and now the new Hyderabad location. Alongside these physical locations, Apple points to its online store, the Apple Store App, and services such as Shop with a Specialist over call or chat as ways customers can connect with products more personally and securely. The company noted that Hyderabad also hosts teams for its Research and Development and Retail Customer Care operations in India.
items.title: Apple Opens First Hyderabad Store on December 10, Reaching Seven Indian Locations
